design.distance: geographic great-circle and each absolute climate-domain difference, ranked within species-calendar-month on identical pair opportunities
design.slope_units: probability percentage points per +10 percentile rank, conditional on all other distance ranks
design.support: previous 1626 species restricted to all six axes jointly identifiable
design.primary: joint five climate domain coefficients; direct thermal minus mean of other four slopes
design.inference: species-equal mean, 5000 whole-genus bootstrap, marginal and simultaneous intervals across seven reported estimates

limitations: Conditional photographic associations, not measured inherited petal morphs or fitness.
Distance ranks represent relative contrasts among sampled observations; they do not compare effects per physical unit.
Separate domain slopes and prior combined climate slope are different estimands.
A positive thermal slope denotes more opposite-colour pairs at larger temperature differences; it does not indicate which colour is favoured.
Fixed source pair graphs share photo vertices and species share spatial settings; whole-genus intervals do not propagate all photographic or spatial uncertainty.
A joint domain coefficient is not a causal climate effect, and the thermal contrast tests mean slopes rather than every possible pairwise difference.
interpretation: On 1618 matched species, geography and annual solar-radiation distance have positive species-equal mean coefficients with simultaneous intervals excluding zero; the solar lower endpoint is close to zero. Thermal-level and temperature-seasonality marginal intervals exclude zero but simultaneous intervals do not. The planned thermal-minus-other-four average contrast is unresolved. This does not establish that solar is stronger than any other domain, or that a majority of species have positive slopes (solar 48.8%). Distance-based divergence differs from the signed mean white fraction-temperature association. The observational photo proxy cannot identify UV protection, pollinator-mediated selection, pigment costs, fitness or genetically inherited polymorphism.
